SMTO-EXE-0172 — SMTO lost contact with the Gateway during a document task

GUID: 9cc29e85-1116-5e6f-bbf2-ee17d7a23763
Slug: office-gateway-lost
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't get an answer from the computer working on your document. SMTO never overwrites the original file, but check whether a new copy was saved before asking again.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways and select Check connection for the Gateway this task used. SMTO needs a working connection to that computer before it can open documents there.
  2. If it can't connect, make sure the Gateway computer is switched on, connected to the network and the Gateway program is running. The Gateway is the helper program SMTO uses to work with files on that computer.
  3. If the connection works, select Check for updates on the same page and install any Gateway update offered. An older Gateway may not understand document requests.
  4. Before asking again, look in the conversation and the document's folder for a newly saved copy. Ask again only if there isn't one. The task may have finished on the Gateway before contact was lost.

What success looks like

  • The Gateway shows as connected and SMTO reports the document result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway computer. Don't ask SMTO to repeat an edit until you've confirmed no new copy was already saved.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Office request or its cancellation did not return a usable result from the selected Gateway: the transport returned an HTTP or outbound-session error (400/404/405/422/501 classify as rejected before dispatch) or the route could not be reached (office.gateway_lost).

What this means

  • Office transport received a Gateway HTTP/control error or could not reach the selected route; the retained phase and effect facts determine whether publication could have occurred. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • Office transport received a Gateway HTTP/control error or could not reach the selected route; the retained phase and effect facts determine whether publication could have occurred.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original operation, source and intended new output path before restoring the same verified Gateway route.

How to fix it

  • Restore the selected Gateway route (Check connection under Settings › Setup › Gateways; a 404/405/501 usually means the Gateway predates the /office/operation endpoint and needs updating). Before issuing a new document-producing request, inspect the source, the run's artifacts or output_path and the retained receipt; do not replay an uncertain write.
  • Restore the intended Gateway route and inspect the original source, output and receipt before another operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Restore the selected Gateway connection and inspect the source and output before a new request.

How to verify the fix

  • The original publication state is established before any new document-producing request.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
